rows.notes: The paper is a conceptual/extension-style piece. Methodology states it is based on 'case studies and conceptual methods' summarising historical information, but no case study data, survey, experiment or model runs are reported; Table 1 is a narrative list of weather-related problems and Figures 2-3 are a screenshot and a conceptual flowchart. No empirical test of a weather-forecasting app or DSS mitigating weather or climate-change impacts; benefits are asserted and illustrated with hypothetical forecast messages. The conclusion recommends a pilot project to test feasibility, confirming no own evidence exists. Rated as not a primary study; even if Q1 were judged 'yes' on the basis of the loosely described case-study analysis, Q2 would still be 'no'.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 53-61). The study offers no quantitative data, uncertainty measures or stated limitations of its own findings; the only conditions stated (farmer training/awareness, cooperation with data users) are recommendations rather than findings.
